Q: Warning: Invalid attribute name: `'data-*'` A:

I think the warning is due to quotes around 'data-name'. It's not TypeScript-specific. To fix, ensure your SVG doesnt contain invalid JSX attributed. Open img.svg and replace any attribute='value' with attribute="value" and remove quotes around attribute names like 'data-name' ->data-name.

Q: Getting access to a binary response byte-by-byte in classic asp/JScript A:

Maybe not quite on the topic, but using VBScript I wrote this:

option explicit
dim fso, wshSHell, objShellApp, args, stdin,stdout

set fso         = CreateObject("Scripting.FileSystemObject")
Set wshShell    = CreateObject("WScript.Shell")
set objShellApp = CreateObject("Shell.Application")
Set args = Wscript.Arguments
set stdin = wscript.stdin
set stdout = wscript.stdout

dim filename, txtFile

filename = args(0)

Const adTypeBinary = 1

'Create Stream object
Dim BinaryStream, data
Set BinaryStream = CreateObject("ADODB.Stream")

'Specify stream type - we want To get binary data.
BinaryStream.Type = adTypeBinary

'Open the stream
BinaryStream.Open

'Load the file data from disk To stream object
BinaryStream.LoadFromFile filename

'Open the stream And get binary data from the object
data = BinaryStream.Read
BinaryStream.close

dim i, item, strLine, hexLine
hexLine = ""
strLine = ""

stdout.writeline "Decimal |Hex     |Data                                             | ASCII 33-254"
for i = 0 to lenb(data)-1
  item = ascb(midb(data,i+1,1))
  if ((i MOD 16) = 0) and (i<>0) then
    stdout.writeLine right("00000000" & i,8) & "|" & right("00000000" & hex(i),8) & "|" &  hexLine & " | " & strLine
    hexLine = ""
    strLine = ""
  end if
  hexLine = hexLine & right("0" & hex(item),2) & " "
  if (item <= 32) or (item > 254) then 
    strLine=strLine + "."
  else
    strLine = strLine & chr(item)
  end if
next

Key to this solution is to know that the variable 'data' contains an array of bytes. You can handle that by using the function lenb (length of byte array) and midb (to extract one or more bytes).

Run the script as follows:

cscript dumphex.vbs my_binary_file.bin > my_binary_file.hex.txt

This will output to standard out the hex code of all the binary file data. Each line of 16 hex codes is prefixed by a decimal + hex counter of the byte number. THe last column displays readable ascii between 33 and 254.

Also great to circumvent that annoying editor that interprets your UTF-8 codes, if you want to see just the exact codes in your ascii files.

Q: Why my website doesn't accept video uploads A:

This doesn't answer your question, but your developer is falling victim to the it works on my machine problem; it's sort of become a meme.

You haven't told us what your position is on your team, so I can only assume you are a QA tester, project manager, or team lead. A team lead is typically an technical expert, so I'm assuming you occupy a non-technical role. Given this, here is an approach to get some headway with the developer:

  • Focus on the symptoms.
  • Present the steps to reproduce the issue in the environment in which you are testing.
  • Take any necessary screenshots or videos to help illustrate the issue.
  • Keep management in the loop.
  • Make sure management is holding developers accountable for all the environments in which code is deployed.
  • If you are on the deployment side of the workforce, that is, you are setting up application environments and deployment pipelines, work directly with the developer to root out a misconfiguration or other environmental problem.

I really can't give you more specific advice unless I know which position you occupy on the team. Knowing your responsibilities and the developer's responsibilities is the key to moving forward. If the developer isn't responsible for the application environment, then the developer can only provide you with some guidance in troubleshooting this.

If nobody is responsible for the application environment, your first order of business is finding someone who can make that decision: who ultimately has the responsibility, and do they have authority over the developer? If not, who has authority over the developer?

Q: Python Selenium with Firefox getting a button click doesn't seem to work A:

A bit inconclusive why you face the DeprecationWarning as the firefox_profile module still works perfecto using the most recent Selenium Version: 4.44.0 which by default uses the inbuilt Selenium Manager and downloads the matching GeckoDriver for Firefox version 151.0.2 (64-bit) on my Windows 11 system.

Minimal Code:

from selenium import webdriver
from selenium.webdriver.firefox.options import Options
from selenium.webdriver.firefox.firefox_profile import FirefoxProfile

options = Options()
firefox_profile = FirefoxProfile()
firefox_profile.set_preference("javascript.enabled", False)
options.profile = firefox_profile
driver = webdriver.Firefox(options=options)
driver.get("file:///D:/My%20Documents/Interview%20Notes/StackOverflow/webpage.html")
